extracted.subtask_description: Reporting on a corporate advertising misstep and the company's press-release response; useful as implicit guidance for crisis communications and PR responses to social-media backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making light of serious issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The company should not 'make light of any serious issue.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pepsi's press release explicitly said: 'We did not intend to make light of any serious issue.' The article presents this as the core complaint that led to the ad being pulled — avoid framing advertising concepts (unity, protest, police encounters) in ways that trivialize real suffering or ongoing social movements. Anti-pattern: using entertainment shorthand for deeply political or traumatic events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and avoid appropriation of social movements
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not appropriate the imagery or message of real protest movements for commercial purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics compared the ad to the image of Ieshia Evans being arrested at a protest and called the commercial 'disrespect and appropriation of a movement.' Guidance implied by the coverage: do not repurpose iconic or painful images/contexts of activism for product promotion; consult with affected communities and subject-matter advisors before using such motifs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure diverse representation in decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Include diverse perspectives in ad development and approvals so issues of race and sensitivity are not overlooked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article quotes Travon Free: 'The Kendall Jenner Pepsi fiasco is a perfect example of what happens when there's no black people in the room when decisions are being made.' Practical guidance: involve diverse creative, marketing, and legal stakeholders to catch tone-deaf ideas early; anti-pattern is homogeneous teams greenlighting insensitive content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-test creative for cultural sensitivity and audience reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Test ads with target demographics and sensitivity readers before wide release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece notes the ad 'was an attempt to reach out to millennials' but 'missed the mark.' Implied best practice: research and pre-testing (focus groups, advisory panels, cultural-sensitivity review) can surface potential offense; failing to pre-test increases risk of large-scale backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor social media and be prepared to act quickly
rubrics_metrics.description: Track online reaction and take timely corrective steps if criticism is intense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following 'intense social media criticism' Pepsi 'yanked the ad.' The article shows the speed and scale of Twitter response (retweets, viral commentary). Guidance: have protocols to monitor platforms, assess harm, and enact corrective measures (remove content, pause rollouts) rapidly to limit damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use press releases to apologize and state remedial actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue a public statement that acknowledges the mistake, apologizes, and outlines corrective steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pepsi's emailed statement: 'Clearly we missed the mark, and we apologize. We did not intend to make light of any serious issue. We are removing the content and halting any further rollout.' This article treats that release as the company's formal response — guidance: be clear, specific about actions (content removal, halted rollouts), and avoid defensive language.
